Subject: Hosting & VPC controls — residency snapshot request

Hi Irene,

Quick one as we move our legal review along: we need a concise evidence snapshot that confirms the following for Redwood's EU hosted offering for Covenant Health (prod workload):

- Tenant traffic and KV/cache persistence do not exit the EU region (routing and egress paths).
- KMS key residency: is customer keying supported (CMK) or Redwood-managed only? If Redwood-managed, what region do keys live in and what evidence can you share?
- PrivateLink / VPC peering topology for EU region (diagram + expected IP ranges).
- SOC 2 scope: which trust services criteria are covered and is a redacted report available?
- CAIQ/SIG answers for data locality controls (any high-risk gaps we should expect).

We'd like an email bundle we can hand to our security team — runbook snippet, a topology diagram, and whatever CAIQ/SIG excerpts relevant to residency. Also include timeline/notes if any fallback routes can send tokens outside EU under failover.

If it's easier, propose a 30-minute call this week with your infra lead + our security engineer.

Thanks,
Peter

Covenant Health

Hi Peter — thanks for the clear ask. Putting a concise packet together now; summary below and I'll attach a downloadable bundle (PDF + topology PNG + CAIQ extract) by EOD. Happy to jump on a quick call if useful — I have 14:30 or 16:00 CET open Wed/Thu.

High-level answers (summary):
- Regional egress: For Redwood EU-hosted clusters we enforce region-local routing by default. Control plane metadata may transit control signals to the control plane in eu-west-1, but customer inference data (requests, KV caches, token payloads) are served from EU-only GPUs and do not traverse non-EU egress under normal operation. We will include the routing matrix and the peering/egress IP ranges in the packet.
- KMS: We support two KMS modes for dedicated/private customers: (1) Redwood-managed keys provisioned and stored in the EU, or (2) customer-managed keys via AWS KMS (customer account) for Dedicated/Private setups. The hosted multi-tenant offering uses Redwood-managed keys unless a dedicated contract and key rotation terms are in place. Evidence: kms-policy-snapshot.txt + KMS residency statement included.
- PrivateLink / VPC peering: see attached privatelink-topology.png and the peer IP range table. On failover the platform will prefer warm-standby within EU; cross-region fallback is only triggered if EU capacity is exhausted and is subject to the customer's routing policy. We'll include the exact fallback policy conditions.
- SOC 2: We can provide a redacted SOC 2 Type II summary for the inference service and a bridge letter describing EU scoping. Full report available under NDA if required — legal can coordinate. Attached: soc2-summary-redacted.pdf.
- CAIQ/SIG: we'll include a pre-filter of CAIQ controls that map to data locality questions and call out any design differences for hosted vs. dedicated/private.

Deliverables (EOD): eu-hosting-evidence.pdf (summary), privatelink-topology.png, kms-policy-snapshot.txt, soc2-summary-redacted.pdf, and a zip with the raw artifacts: evidence-package-eu-20250630.zip.

Next steps: please confirm whether Covenant requires a customer-managed KMS (we can propose a migration pathway) and whether you want our legal team to send the DPA + SOC2 NDA for the full report.

Thanks — Icc
Irene Choi
Senior Security PM, Redwood Inference

On Mon, Jun 30, 2025 at 13:19 Peter Lowe <peter.lowe@covenanthealth.com> wrote:
> Irene — quick clarification: Covenant prefers customer-managed keys for prod. Two quick Qs:
>
> 1) If we require CMK in our AWS account, does Redwood support Bring-Your-Own-KMS for the hosted offering or only for Dedicated/Private?

Short answer: BYOK is supported only for Dedicated and Private deployments where the customer supplies the KMS in their account or HSM. For our standard hosted multi-tenant offering we currently provide Redwood-managed keys (stored in EU). If BYOK is a hard requirement, the supported path is Dedicated capacity or Private deployment; we can provide a migration and onboarding checklist for CMK. See kms-policy-snapshot.txt for the precise scope and key rotation cadence.

> 2) In the fallback policy you mentioned, what concrete signals trigger cross-region failover? Our reviewers want the specific capacity/health thresholds or an explicit human-in-the-loop escalation.

Concrete triggers (excerpt from runbook included):
- Autoscaler saturation: sustained enqueue latency > 2x SLO for 3 minutes AND queue depth > 95th percentile for 2 consecutive minutes.
- Node health: > 30% unhealthy GPU instances for 5 minutes in a single AZ AND control-plane reconciliation failures > 2 attempts.
- Manual override: operator-issued fallback for incident mitigation (audit trail required).
Fallback to non-EU capacity (only as a last-resort) is subject to the customer's routing policy — we will never send production inference data outside the EU unless the customer has explicitly accepted a fallback policy that allows cross-region routing in the contract. This is included in the EU hosting evidence PDF and the runbook snippet inside the zip.

I have attached the evidence bundle to this message (attachment stubs listed below). If you'd like, let's lock 16:00 CET Wed — I can have Karthik on the call to walk the topology and Marissa can cover DPA/contract path for BYOK.

Best,
Irene
